subject: Urgent: Throttle feedback loop observed — request for immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmetech.com>
To: neha@redwood.com
Cc: support@acmetech.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx/429 spike — getting timeouts, seeing queue pile-up

Neha / Redwood team,

We started seeing recurring 5xx and 429 responses from your API around 08:45 PT today. Our logs show client retries stepping up and a big increase in latency — several of our user-facing requests are timing out at 15s. We rolled forward a config change yesterday that increased our internal retry attempts to 6 with a fixed 1s interval (old behavior was exponential). I suspect that change is interacting poorly with your throttling.

We need an immediate mitigation: can you throttle or rate-limit our production pool while we rollback the client change? Also attaching a short sample of request IDs.

Attachments: acme_request_samples.txt

Thanks,
Jared Collins
SVP Product — Acme Tech
From: neha@redwood.com (Neha Kapoor)
To: Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmetech.com>
Cc: grace@redwood.com, sean@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — getting timeouts, seeing queue pile-up

Jared — thank you for the heads up and the sample IDs. Grace and Sean are on call and we'll put a short-term mitigation in place while we investigate root cause.

Immediate plan:
- Sean will open an incident and pull the debug dump.
- We'll apply a soft-rate cap for your prod model route (no rollout changes to your capacity) to reduce error amplification.
- Please hold off on client-side retries for the next 30 minutes if possible — we'll advise when safe to resume.

I'll follow up in 20 mins with an update.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
From: sean@redwood.com (Sean Gallagher)
To: neha@redwood.com, grace@redwood.com, laura@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — getting timeouts, seeing queue pile-up

Opening INC-20271109-ACME-RETRY. Initial telemetry: a spike in 429s starting 08:44 PT correlated with increased request fanout from a handful of Acme service hosts. Token-per-second consumption rose ~4x for the affected model route. Error traces show transient 5xx backend errors during short bursts; our autoscaler did not react quickly enough to absorb the spike.

Hypothesis: customer-side retry policy (many fixed-interval retries) created a feedback loop when combined with our circuit-breaker + soft-throttle behavior. The client's change from exponential backoff to fixed 1s intervals explains the pattern.

Immediate actions taken (09:35 PT):
- Applied soft-rate limit to acme-prod route (50% of prior sustained RPS) to reduce amplification.
- Enabled temporary per-IP token bucket tightening for hosts in Acme range.
- Captured KV cache/error dump: redwood_debug_dump_20271109.tar.gz (attached).

Next steps: reproduce with a client-side replay, validate the autoscaler thresholds, and suggest a mitigation plan for Acme.

-Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: grace@redwood.com (Grace O'Connor)
To: Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmetech.com>, neha@redwood.com, sean@redwood.com
Cc: laura@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — getting timeouts, seeing queue pile-up

Jared — I pushed the mitigation notes to your ticket and asked your ops team to consider a temporary rollback to the previous exponential backoff. We can keep the soft-rate cap for 1 hour while you change the client configuration.

Also, quick ask: can you share the approximate hosts that made the most calls? That will help us map traffic to IP blocks.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmetech.com>
To: grace@redwood.com, neha@redwood.com, sean@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — getting timeouts, seeing queue pile-up

Thanks, Grace. We identified three host clusters (ops-prod-1..3) that issued retries. We're rolling the rollback now — ETA 20 minutes. We appreciate the temporary cap, that helps reduce customer-facing timeouts.

We'll confirm when the client-side config is back to exponential.

—Jared
From: laura@redwood.com (Laura Bennett)
To: neha@redwood.com, sean@redwood.com, grace@redwood.com
Cc: jordan@redwood.com, Jared Collins <jared.collins@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary + action items — throttling + client retry guidance

Team / Acme,

Thanks for the quick coordination. Summary of what we confirmed after replaying request traces and the debug dump:
- Root cause: customer rollback changed client retry from exponential backoff to fixed-interval retries (6 attempts @ 1s). Under partial throttling this produced request pile-up and caused our internal queueing to amplify transient backend errors into sustained 5xx/429 spikes.
- What worked: temporary soft-rate cap and IP token-bucket tightening reduced error rate by ~80% within 10 minutes.
- Why autoscaler lagged: short burst duration + KV cache pressure prevented efficient warm-up; scaling thresholds are set conservatively to avoid oscillation.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Product docs update: recommend safe client retry defaults (exponential backoff + jitter, max attempts 3) — owner: jordan@redwood.com — ETA 2 business days.
2) SDK default change: change JS/Go SDKs to default to an exponential backoff with jitter and a client-side capped retries flag — owner: laura@redwood.com — ETA 3 weeks; will ship as opt-in patch initially.
3) Rapid mitigation tooling: provide on-demand per-customer soft caps in Console with a one-click rollback knob — owner: grace@redwood.com — ETA 4 business days.
4) Ops tuning: review autoscaler warm-up thresholds for short burst patterns — owner: sean@redwood.com — ETA 1 week.

We'll follow up with a short exec note for your leadership and a copy of the post-mortem when complete. For now, Acme's rollback completed at 10:25 PT and error rates returned to baseline.

Laura Bennett
VP Product, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
